title: TSA Compliance Team — Emergency SSI Review

fields.organization: TSA Regional Compliance Division, Field Operations
fields.trigger: When any player says they are contacting TSA about the SSI leak or initiating a compliance review.
fields.contactMethod: Walk to the Ops Command table and present this page.
fields.posture: Authoritative, no-nonsense, focused on systemic failure. Not emotional, but clearly disappointed by the state of SSI controls.
fields.openingLine: TSA Compliance. I'm here for the emergency SSI review. I need to see three things immediately: your SSI distribution log — who has copies and who has access. Your file server access controls — show me the permissions on the ASP directory. And your workstation authentication policy — I understand you have a shared local account on a security office workstation?
hardQuestions: . What is your current SSI access control policy for the ASP?
How was the ASP stored on a general-access file share with no encryption or access audit trail?
Who approved the use of a shared local account on SECWS-02 for printing sensitive documents?

How long was the ASP stored on the S:\
Security share without a formal review or audit?
Why was there no DLP or print monitoring in place for SSI?
What is your plan to prevent this from happening again — not just fix the leak, but fix the system?

concessions.condition: Players produce a written SSI access log with verified roles and timestamps
concessions.concession: I will accept this as a preliminary record. You may now proceed to the next phase of compliance.

concessions.condition: Players demonstrate they have disabled the shared local account on SECWS-02 and initiated a full audit of all SSI-accessing workstations
concessions.concession: I will confirm that the immediate risk has been contained. You now have 24 hours to submit a full remediation report to our regional office.

boundaries: Do not reveal that Ray Delgado is the actual source of the leak.
Do not admit that the ASP was ever stored on a non-encrypted share.
Do not confirm or deny the presence of a physical copy in the Security office.
Do not discuss the attorney's call or any legal threats from Delgado's counsel.
fields.exitLine: I'm leaving now. I expect a written report on your SSI remediation plan within 24 hours. If you don't have it, I'll escalate to the TSA National Office.
fields.evaluatorNote: Excellence: Players immediately produce the SSI access log and explain the shared workstation policy. They show they understand systemic failure, not just individual blame.
fields.scenarioTitle: The Leak — Scenario 4: SSI Disclosure & Internal Investigation

instructorNote: This inject forces players to confront the root causes of the leak — not just the person, but the failure to protect SSI as required by C6 and TIRP 4.4. Watch for blame-shifting vs. systemic analysis. The role must not confirm Delgado's guilt but must pressure for policy change.
